title: Irregularities & discrepancies flagged for review
method: Anything observed that is inconsistent, stale, impossible, or a structural risk gets a numbered entry here and is never silently normalized. Severity: high = affects trust in a result; medium = affects interpretation; low = cosmetic/monitor.

items.title: Election Assistance Commission has had NO serving commissioners since July 2026
items.detail: Two of three commissioners were dismissed by the president and the remaining one resigned, leaving the federal election-administration commission without a member (Wikipedia, fetched 2026-09-18; Ballotpedia corroborates leadership history). Its guidance output is at risk until reconstituted.

items.title: Shared API host returned STALE last_price_dollars / updated_time for CONTROLH-2026

The order-book fields (yes_bid/yes_ask) were current. This session's snapshot uses the order-book side and flags the divergence.

items.title: KXMUSKCHALLENGERS-26: 'At least 3' (13%) priced ABOVE 'At least 1' (12%) — logically impossible
items.detail: The event 'How many Elon-backed challengers will win seats in Congress this year?' shows the 'at least 3' outcome at 13% while 'at least 1' sits at 12%. Since {at least 3} ⊂ {at least 1}, this ordering cannot hold for consistent probabilities. Likely a thin market with a wide/stale book.
items.action: Flagged, not traded in any strategy; monitor for self-correction. If it persists into the 2026 cycle it is a candidate for a market-design anomaly study.

items.title: Election-day (2024-11-05) candlestick bar was not captured for the 2024 backtest markets
items.detail: The historical candlestick fetch used end_ts=1730851200 (2024-11-05T00:00Z), so the last captured bar is the Nov 4 trading day (bars end at midnight ET). Settlement outcomes come from the official market objects, so backtest conclusions are unaffected, but the final-day price path is missing from the charts.
items.action: Collectors re-fetch with end_ts = settlement_ts + 86400; until then the site labels the last point as '2024-11-04 (last captured bar)'.

items.title: Poll margin -> win probability uses a logistic mapping (k=4.5) that is a labeled assumption, not a published 538 probability
items.detail: 538's public archive publishes margins, not probabilities. This repo maps margin m to p = 1/(1+exp(-m/4.5)) (the scaling 538 used in its 2020 national model) and labels every use as 'modeled mapping'.
items.action: Sensitivity: at k=3 the same 2024-09-12 anchor (Harris +2.82) implies 31% for Trump instead of 35%; the poll-vs-market gap conclusion is unchanged.

items.title: Kalshi prices 7 of 13 rated 2026 Senate races outside the bands implied by BOTH Cook and Inside Elections ratings (all in the Democratic direction)
items.detail: 2026-09-19 tracker vs Cook (Sep 15) / Inside Elections (Sep 17): AK D 68.5% (Toss Up / Tilt R), ME D 67.5% (Toss Up / Toss-up), NH D 83.5% (Toss Up / Toss-up), GA D 93.7% (Lean D / Tilt D), NC D 92.4% (Lean D / Tilt D), KS D 26.5% (Likely R / Likely R), NE Osborn (I) 31.5% (Likely R / Likely R). Either the market is ahead of the raters in a D+8–13 generic-ballot environment or it is overconfident; the 2024 backtest cannot distinguish these yet. Poll cross-check added later on 2026-09-19: the only public AK poll captured (NYT/Siena, released Jul 1: Sullivan 47 – Peltola 45) implies D ≈ 39% vs the market's 68.5%; for OH (special) NYT/Siena Jul 1 had Husted 50 – Brown 47 (D ≈ 34%) vs a 54.5% market. Both polls are 11 weeks old, so the gap mixes time drift with disagreement.
items.action: Published in the poll layer (ratingsComparison) for human review; re-evaluated automatically each day. Settlements on Nov 3 2026 will score it.

items.title: Iowa Senate: Emerson (Aug 31–Sep 1) R+5 implies D ≈ 25% under the project's logistic mapping; Kalshi prices Turek (D) at 39.5%
items.detail: The 14.7-point gap is the largest of the five poll-vs-market comparisons made first (ME +1.4, MI −1.6/+3.6, TX +2.0). Update 2026-09-19 (later the same day): Suffolk (Aug 20–23, n=500 LV, ±4.4; press-release PDF) has Hinson 45 – Turek 41 → D ≈ 29% under the same mapping (gap +10.4), and NYT/Siena (released Jul 1) had Hinson 48 – Turek 46 → D ≈ 39% (gap +0.4). The market (39.5%) therefore sits between the three polls' implied values; Emerson is the most Republican-leaning of the three, not evidence of a market anomaly on its own. The Texas Poll/ReconMR (Talarico +6 → 79%) vs market 57.5% (gap −21.6) is now the largest single-poll gap; two Texas polls disagree with each other (Emerson Talarico +1).
items.action: Transcribed Suffolk and NYT/Siena Iowa toplines (data/polls/poll-layer-2026.json). Keep reading multi-poll gaps, not single-poll gaps; a poll average per race is the next step (ROADMAP R4).

items.title: 207 traded markets returned inside OPEN events were already settled (status=finalized, results known) — trading had ended weeks earlier, yet they sat in the 'open' universe and, unguarded, would have entered the calibration sample as perfectly-priced post-settlement observations
items.detail: Daily capture 2026-09-19 (GET /events?status=open&with_nested_markets=true): 207 of 10,915 traded markets had close_time < capture time (17 in July, 102 in August, 88 in September 2026), yes_bid 0 / yes_ask 1 and last prices pinned near 0.01 or 0.99 (e.g. KXBERNIEENDORSE-26NOV03-ADEL closed 2026-07-14, KXTRUMPMEETING-27JAN01-NCSHE closed 2026-07-19 at 0.998, KXHORMUZNORM-26MAR17-B260715 closed 2026-07-21 with 2.18M volume). Multi-market events stay 'open' until every rung settles, so closed rungs are nested in open events. The first-day files did not record the per-market status field, so whether the exchange reports them as 'closed' or still 'active' is unknown until the next live run. None of them is a 2026 general-election race market. The Python sample (top 2,000 by volume) contained none because its filter reads status directly. Update (live run 35412822292, 01:30 UTC the same day, after the status column was added): the API reports all 207 as status=finalized with official results — 174 no, 33 yes; settlement_ts between 2026-07-13 and 2026-09-18. Before the guard, the first scorer pass pooled their post-settlement prices (170 observations in the 0–10% bucket with 0% YES) — a look-ahead artefact, not calibration evidence.
items.action: Fixed: finalized rungs are recorded once in tracker/settlements.json (with settlement_ts and result) and excluded from the daily CSV; closed-pending rungs keep their status; src/calibration.js ignores any price row with a non-active status and any observation dated on/after the settlement day (scoreableMarkets / observationsExcludedAsLookAhead are reported). Site: 'settlements on file' table, run log, 'past close' chips. Still open: why finalized rungs remain nested in status=open events (Kalshi API semantics) — documented in LIMITATIONS.

items.title: 270toWin renders Kalshi probabilities from LAST TRADES ('may not total 100%') — matched against this project's two API captures within 1¢
items.detail: Fetched 2026-09-19: 270towin.com carries a 'Prediction Markets' block reading 'Which party will win the 2028 Presidential Election?' with the values '57%' and '41%', a Kalshi logo, and the disclosure 'Probability based on the most recent ‘yes’ trade for each party as of Sep. 19, 2026 at 18:17 UTC (2:17 PM EDT). May not total 100%.' The same two tickers in this project's independent captures of that day — Node events feed stamped 2026-09-19T15:59:45Z (data/kalshi/tracker/daily/2026-09-19.csv) and Python markets feed stamped 2026-09-19T15:59:58Z (data/kalshi/markets_politics_latest.json) — both read KXPRESPARTY-2028-D bid 0.58 / ask 0.59 / last 0.58 and KXPRESPARTY-2028-R bid 0.41 / ask 0.42 / last 0.41. The rendered 41% equals the Republican last trade exactly and 57% sits 1¢ below the Democratic last trade captured 2h18m earlier; which figure belongs to which party is an INFERENCE from that match, because the page does not label them. The pair sums to 98%, consistent with the page's own disclaimer and with #7. Freshness is mixed on one page: the market panel is same-day while the 2024-margin base map is stamped 'Map Updated: Jan. 29, 2025 at 12:53 UTC'.
items.action: Treat third-party renderings of Kalshi prices as a CORROBORATION surface only. They corroborate this project’s captures to within 1¢, but they are last-trade based, may not sum to 100%, and can mix capture dates on a single page. Every price used in models, backtests and the contest continues to come from yes_bid/yes_ask captured directly from the API (see #2).

items.detail: Fetched 2026-09-19: https://www.selzerco.com/ returned only navigation scaffolding ('Skip to primary navigation', 'Skip to content', '## Main Content', 'Menu') with no substantive content, so nothing could be verified from the pollster's own site. items.title: Method-mixing risk: a non-probability / post-stratification pollster now sits in the master list beside probability panels

items.action: Fixed: the raw directory is created up front, and each target is wrapped so a crash becomes a verdict:'error' row ('probe crashed: …') instead of aborting the run — verified locally end-to-end (24 targets). (2) Collector: a pre-write self-consistency guard now throws when bySeries totals do not reconcile with the projected event list, so an internally inconsistent universe can never be written again. (3) Workflow: the commit step takes a sha256 anchor of the collector's output files after all data steps (kanchor) and, after ANY rebase, re-hashes them and — if they changed — re-captures, re-runs pipeline/lint/tests and amends the commit, so what gets pushed is always one consistent run's snapshot. items.detail: Direct fetches 2026-09-21 transcribed toplines for GA governor (Jackson 48 / Bottoms 45), GA Senate (Ossoff 51 / Collins 42), SC Senate (Graham 48 / Andrews 43), AK Senate (Sullivan 39 / Peltola 39, four-candidate RCV ballot) and the generic ballot (D 49 / R 41). The SC release's biographical framing — 'the seat formerly held by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham', an appointment narrative — is the publisher's own and is NOT corroborated by this project; the AK release hinges on a two-candidate read of a four-candidate RCV ballot. Candidate identity itself is corroborated exactly against the exchange: SENATESC-26 yes_sub_titles 'Darline Graham'/'Annie Andrews' and vote-share markets KXVOTEGENERAL-SENATESC-26DGRA/-AAND; GOVPARTYGA-26 RJAC/KBOT; SENATEGA-26 Ossoff/Collins. The ingested SC margin (R+5 → mapped D p≈0.248) sits far below the captured SENATESC-26-D market (~0.13-0.14) — a genuine poll-vs-market divergence the dashboard now displays; GA Senate shows the mirror image (poll-implied D 0.881 vs market ~0.932). items.title: The 2026 control markets do NOT resolve on a simple majority-plus-VP rule — the official rule names the President pro tempore / the Speaker on February 1 of the following year, and permits an early media-call determination
items.detail: Fetched 2026-09-22 from GET /markets?series_ticker=CONTROLS|CONTROLH. CONTROLS-2026-D rules_primary: 'If the Democratic Party has won control of the U.S. Senate in 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.' rules_secondary: 'This market may be determined early based on a consensus of media calls projecting control of the U.S. Senate. See full rules for details. Otherwise, victory will be determined by the party identification of the President pro tempore of the Senate on February 1, 2027.' CONTROLH-2026-R rules_secondary names 'the party identification of the Speaker of the House on February 1, 2027'. Both markets carry close_time 2027-02-01T15:00:00Z and settlement_timer_seconds 3600. The session-11 handoff (NEXT_SESSION.md item 1) had queued the task as 'confirm majority(51) + VP tiebreak' — that reading is NOT what the exchange publishes, and control of a chamber is a different event from a 51-seat majority (it tracks the presiding officer's party, which can differ from the seat count during a vacancy or an organising dispute).
items.action: Recorded the captured rule text verbatim in data/sources/master.json entry `kalshi-market-rules`. Do NOT set controlQuestion.resolutionRule.confirmed=true from the queued majority assumption: nothing in this repo may assert a resolution rule that was not read from the exchange. The cross-layer control questions and any seat-count arithmetic must state that the resolved event is the presiding officer's party on 2027-02-01, with an early media-call determination permitted.

items.title: The Leap's contest parameters are per-edition — the $100,000 bankroll and the 3-day minimum are one edition's rules, not a universal template
items.detail: The official rules page for the February 2026 Eurex edition states a minimum of 'trading activity for at least 3 days' and ranks by realized profit/loss on closed positions, with all open positions automatically closed at the end. The May 2026 crypto edition's own leaderboard implies a $100,000 bankroll arithmetically: for Manishh_jain92 the page shows +$271,783.86 and +271.78%, i.e. 271783.86 / 2.7178 = 100,001.42; four further top-10 rows reproduce the same figure to within $3 (Sistem_Akinci_1453, MarketMaverick007, thethuthiem, Snipercoopz). Separately, the July 2026 TradeStation edition is reported at $100,000 with a 5-day minimum, and the September 2026 AMP Futures edition at $250,000 with a 5-day minimum — so balance and minimum days both vary by edition.
items.action: The live 2026 season is published with $100,000 and a 3-day minimum, and the artifact states the edition it copies (`model.leapSource`). The Next-session list records that edition parameters must be re-read from the then-current official rules before any parameter is reused, and that the site must never describe $100,000/3-day as 'the Leap's rules' without the edition qualifier.

items.title: The live 2026 season ranks on mark-to-market net equity and applies two Kalshi-specific rules The Leap does not have — both are disclosed adaptations
items.detail: The Leap ranks on realized P/L on closed positions with everything auto-closed at the end. A live Kalshi election season runs for months with unsettled markets, so the 2026 leaderboard is published as net equity = cash + open positions marked to the captured bid/ask midpoint, with the label 'marked to the <date> capture — NOT a final result'. Two further rules exist only because the universe is ~1,000 traded election markets per day rather than one instrument: a fill is capped at 10% of the day's volume and 10% of open interest, and gross NEW deployment per day is capped at 20% of start-of-day equity, allocated pro-rata across that day's orders. Without the second rule a bankroll-relative order size is consumed by whichever market the loop happened to reach first.
items.action: Published in the season artifact (`model.dailyDeploymentNote`, `model.execution`, `model.marks`, `model.ranking`) and on the site, each labelled ADAPTATION rather than a Leap rule. When all 2026 markets have settled, net equity converges to realized P/L and the two definitions agree; until then the leaderboard header says so.

items.title: Kalshi's fee schedule gives the MAKER default multiplier as 0, while src/fees.js documents a single default of 1
items.detail: The official fee schedule PDF (fetched 2026-09-22, 'Fee Schedule for July 2026 — 7.7.26 Update') states for taker fees 'M = the multiplier for each contract (default is 1 unless otherwise indicated)' and, separately, for maker fees 'M = the multiplier for each contract (default is 0 unless otherwise indicated)'. src/fees.js transcribes only the taker wording into its header comment. The taker arithmetic itself is exact (the PDF's formula round up(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1-P)) matches the code verbatim), and every one of the 1,413 US-election series in the captured registry carries fee_multiplier 1, so no published number is affected.
items.action: RESOLVED 2026-09-22: makerFee uses coefficient 0.0175 and maker M defaults to 0. The captured fee_multiplier is the taker multiplier and is not copied onto maker M. quadratic_with_maker_fees without an explicit maker multiplier stays maker M 0 and is labelled unstated. The contest remains taker-only.

items.title: `close_time` is the exchange's listing-expiry / cycle field, NOT the date a market resolves — it lands a year after the event it is about
items.detail: Every open politics/elections market in the 2026-09-21 capture carries a close_time, but the field does not mean what its name suggests. The 2026 Alaska Senate market SENATEAK-26-D (“Democratic party”) carries close_time 2027-11-03 — 365 days after the 2026 election it is about — and SENATEKS-26-R carries the same. The 2028-cycle markets already listed for trading (SENATEIN-28-R, SENATECT-28-D, SENATENV-28-R) carry 2029-11-07, again a year after their election. The full 24,102-row capture distributes as 2026: 859, 2027: 21,261, 2028: 959, 2029: 719, with tails out to 2099. So the field is a cycle/listing-expiry timestamp, and it is only coincidentally a determination date where the rules set one: CONTROLH-2026-D and CONTROLS-2026-D carry 2027-02-01, which IS their stated determination date (party of the Speaker / President pro tempore on February 1, 2027 — irregularity #72). Two consequences follow. (1) Using close_time as a settlement clock would settle 2026 races a year early and can never be trusted. (2) Using it as an eligibility bound without a window would pull 2028-cycle races (1,982 rows of this capture sit after 2027-12-31) into a 2026 season where a days-to-election model is meaningless.
items.action: Handled structurally rather than by patching rows. src/contest/forward-universe.js documents the finding at the constant and scopes the season with SEASON.closesBy = '2027-12-31T23:59:59Z' — a CYCLE bound, not a clock — and the contest settles a position ONLY on a captured official result (data/kalshi/tracker/settlements.json), never on this field. The exclusion is published, not silent: the market list reports close_time-after-window as its own eligibility reason (`closes-after-season-window`, 177 rows on 2026-09-21) and the site prints the reason next to the count. Any future feature that needs a real resolution date must read the settlement feed, not close_time.

items.title: Forward-contest fee registration counted series as captured while registerSeriesFees silently skipped every config
items.detail: scripts/run-forward-contest.mjs passed { multiplier, type } into registerSeriesFees, which only reads fee_multiplier, so the call returned 0 while the runner incremented captured before the call and published 4185. feeProvenance reads that pre-call count, so the season claimed every series had a captured multiplier when none had been registered. The 2024 contest already passed fee_multiplier and was unaffected. Confirmed against data/kalshi/universe/series.json capturedAt 2026-09-21T18:16:44.622Z: 4185 series, all quadratic with a numeric fee_multiplier. No fill in the season used one of the 10 series whose captured multiplier is 0, so published PnL did not move when registration started applying the captured multipliers.
items.action: RESOLVED 2026-09-22: the runner now passes fee_type and fee_multiplier, uses the registration return, and throws if that return is not the count of series with a numeric multiplier. registerSeriesFees throws when multiplier or type is present without a numeric fee_multiplier, so the silent skip cannot recur. A config that already has a numeric fee_multiplier is accepted.
